title: Petra and the Letter
premise: In the winter of 1891, apprentice clockmaker Sebastian Marchetti is summoned to repair the observatory's failing master clock, where he discovers a child abandoned at the door with a note instructing him to forget her face. The girl, Petra, carries a letter that implicates Sebastian's estranged family in a smuggling ring operating beneath the city's clock towers, forcing him to weigh loyalty to the uncle who raised him against the truth the letter reveals. As the river ice begins to crack and authorities close in, Sebastian must decide who gets the last berth on the escape boat — and in the end, he gives it to Petra, sending his uncle's confession downriver instead, choosing truth and belonging over blood.
about_author: Elodie Lockridge is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing clockmakers' ledgers in municipal collections across northern Europe. She writes historical fiction about the small, precise people history forgets to record.

chapters.title: The Weight of Small Gears
chapters.summary: POV Sebastian. Summoned to the observatory on the coldest night of the year, Sebastian works alone on the master clock, establishing his careful, invisible life and his loyalty to Uncle Aldo, who took him in after his parents drowned. Emotional beat: quiet loneliness disguised as contentment.

chapters.title: A Knock at the Observatory Door
chapters.summary: POV Sebastian. At dawn, Sebastian finds a shivering girl, Petra, asleep on the step with a sealed letter pinned to her coat instructing him to forget her face. Unable to leave her in the cold, he hides her among the clockworks. Emotional beat: reluctant tenderness breaking through his guardedness.

chapters.title: What the Letter Said
chapters.summary: POV Sebastian, with a brief flashback in Aldo's voice. Sebastian breaks the seal and learns the letter names his uncle as the paymaster of a smuggling ring moving contraband through clock-tower crypts — and names Petra as the daughter of a man Aldo betrayed. Emotional beat: the ground shifting under everything he believes.

chapters.title: The Face He Was Told to Forget
chapters.summary: POV Petra. Petra wakes among ticking gears and, trusting the boy who fed her, reveals fragments: her father's workshop, men in the night, her mother's whispered instruction to run. Emotional beat: a child's fierce, fragile courage, and Sebastian's growing resolve.

chapters.title: Confrontation at the Marchetti Bench
chapters.summary: POV Sebastian. Sebastian confronts Aldo, who neither denies nor confesses, only warns that the men in the letter will come for the girl and anyone shielding her. Emotional beat: love and betrayal tangled; Sebastian leaves without an answer.

chapters.title: The Ice Begins to Talk
chapters.summary: POV Sebastian. Strangers question the observatory keeper; a smuggler's note appears on Sebastian's workbench. He learns the river will break in days and that the last ferry berth before the thaw is already spoken for — by Aldo, fleeing. Emotional beat: dread tightening into a deadline.

chapters.title: What Petra Remembers
chapters.summary: POV Petra. Hiding in the clock tower, Petra recalls the final night at home and identifies one of the searching men as her father's partner — proof the letter is true. Sebastian realizes memory itself is the only evidence that matters. Emotional beat: memory as burden and gift.

chapters.title: The Confession in the Clockwork
chapters.summary: POV Sebastian. Aldo, cornered by his own partners, comes to the tower to take the letter and the girl. In the dark among the gears, he finally confesses — and begs Sebastian's silence as the loyalty he owes his family. Emotional beat: the climax of loyalty versus truth.

chapters.title: The Last Berth
chapters.summary: POV Sebastian. At the breaking ice, Sebastian makes his choice: he puts Petra on the boat with the letter as her protection and testimony, and lets Aldo face the men and magistrates on shore. Emotional beat: grief, resolve, and the cost of doing right.

chapters.title: The Clock Keeps Time Without Him
chapters.summary: POV Sebastian, epilogue-like. The master clock runs true again; Sebastian takes Petra's promised letter of thanks from downriver, and the observatory keeper offers him the permanent post he never thought he deserved. Emotional beat: belonging earned, not inherited — quiet hope.
